Grill it at home or ask a market vendor to point you to a nearby grill spot.

row.locality_or_neighbourhood: 10 Rue Saint-Pantaléon, historic centre (near Place du Capitole)
row.why_it_is_special: A specialist boutique dedicated to Toulouse's floral emblem. The shop stocks candies, liqueurs, jams, and cosmetics — all violet-based.

row.name: Basilique Saint-Sernin
row.why_it_is_special: Built between 1070 and 1300, it is the largest Romanesque church in Europe. Its 115-metre length, five naves, 64-metre transept, and more than 400 sculpted capitals make it an architectural masterpiece and a key stop on the Santiago de Compostela pilgrimage route.

row.name: Fénétra
row.locality_or_neighbourhood: 2 Rue Ozenne, Carmes quarter (also at 3 Place du Capitole)
row.why_it_is_special: A Toulouse pâtisserie founded in 1967, now with seven shops across the city. Fénétra is a medieval-origin tart layered with shortcrust pastry, almond cream, candied apricot, and candied lemon — traditionally baked for the Fête de la Fénétra in late June. Maison Pillon prepares it canonically, as it has been made for decades.

row.name: Couvent des Jacobins

The convent houses the relics of Saint Thomas Aquinas and hosts concerts and exhibitions in its cloister and refectory.
